The reversible (16,6,2) difference set on (Z/4)^2 gives a real even Fourier sign with every normalized coefficient ±1/4 (independently enumerated all 16 characters). Tensoring gives s_j(-z)=s_j(z), s_j(0)=1 and q_j=4^j. The local density f_j=1+a b_j(w)cos(pi t/2)+i a q_j 1_{w=0}sin(pi t/2) has Fourier support {0}∪{(s_j(z),z)} with coefficients a s_j(z)/q_j, and each nonzero local set is disjoint from its negative. For 0<a≤1/2, the strictly positive p_j=1+a b_j cos has independent bounded g_j with Haar means 0 versus rho means a²/2; dyadic Chebyshev–Borel–Cantelli yields mutually singular infinite product rho and Haar. Because sum_j ||f_j−p_j||_1=a/6, L¹(rho) product perturbations converge to complex singular mass-one mu with exact Fourier support and variation norm ≤exp(a/6). Parseval gives ∥mu*mu∥₂²=∏(1+a⁴/16^j). If gamma has finite block support, E∩(gamma−E) is finite, since every outside block must vanish; character twists and total-variation L¹ approximation then prove |alpha|*|beta| absolutely continuous for every alpha,beta∈M_E. Finite computations corroborate the seed and do not replace the infinite proof.
